U n i t e d I n d i a I n s u r a n c e C o . L t d v s
Smt.Kandukuribaindlalaxmamma And 5 ... on 10 January, 2025

The Honourable Smt. Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1711 of 2018
 And
 Cross-Objections No.27 of 2024
Common Judgment

:
1. Aggrieved by the decree and judgment dated 13.11.2017 passed in M.V.O.P.No.245 of 2012, on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-XIV Additional District & Sessions Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar (for short, 'the Tribunal'), M.A.C.M.A.1711 of 2018 is filed by the Respondent No.3/Insurance Company seeking to allow the Appeal by setting aside the order of the learned Tribunal.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-XIV Additional District & Sessions Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Also, dissatisfied with the compensation granted by the learned Tribunal, the Petitioners in the said O.P. filed Cross Objections No.27 of 2024 seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter be referred as they were arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioners, who are the wife, minor children and mother of Late Kandukuri (Baindla) Narender, (hereinafter be referred as 'the deceased') filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in a road traffic accident that occurred on 05.05.2011 at 11.30 a.m.

It MGP,J MACMA.1711 of 2018 and X-obj.27 of 2024 is stated by the petitioners that on 05.05.2011 at 11.30 a.m., when the deceased along with petitioner Nos.1 to 3 were proceeding in an Auto bearing No.AP-24-W-1618 from Yacharam to Mall and when they reached near Mall Village i.e. near Andhra Bank, the driver of the said Auto drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner due to which the Auto turned turtle and the petitioners fell down.
The deceased-K.Narender received severe bleeding injury to his Head and other parts of the body and the petitioners 1 to 3 sustained minor injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Osmania General Hospital for treatment and he died while undergoing treatment.

4. Based on a complaint, Police of Yacharam Police Station registered a case in Crime No.65 of 2011 under Section 337 IPC, conducted investigation and laid charge sheet under Ex.A2 against the driver of the subject Auto.

It is stated by the petitioners that prior to accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and used to earn Rs.300/- to Rs.400/- per day, approximately Rs.10,000/- per month by working as Agricultural labour and also Drum beating.

On account of sudden death of the deceased,
the petitioners lost their source of income, suffered mental agony and hardship and hence filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- against Respondent Nos.1 to 3 jointly ad severally.

Before the Tribunal, respondent Nos.1 & 2 remained ex- parte.

6. Respondent No.3/Insurance Company filed its counter denying the averments made in the claim petition and further contended that there is no negligence on pat of driver of Auto and that the compensation claimed is excess and exorbitant and prayed to dismiss the claim against it.
It also filed additional counter stating that the driver of the crime Auto do not possess valid driving license to drive the said vehicle.

7. Based on the above pleadings, the learned Tribunal had framed the following issues:-
i. Whether the deceased -K.Narender died in a Motor Vehicle accident on 05.05.2011 due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Auto bearing No.AP-24-W-1618 by its driver?
ii. What was the age and income of the deceased?
iii. Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation and if so, how much amount and from which of the respondents?
iv. To what relief?
8. Before the Tribunal, the petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased examined herself as PW1, got examined PW2 and got marked Exs.A1 to A5 on their behalf.
MGP,J MACMA.1711 of 2018 and X-obj.27 of 2024 9.
On behalf of respondent No.3/Insurance Company, RW1 was examined and ExsB1 to B9 were marked.

10. After considering the entire evidence and documents marked by both sides, the learned Tribunal had partly- allowed the claim petition of the petitioners by awarding compensation of Rs.4,89,000/-
along with future interest @ 9% per annum payable by Respondent Nos.1 & 3 jointly and severally.
Aggrieved with the said finding, the respondent No.3 in the O.P./Insurance Company filed M.A.C.M.A.No.1711 of 2018 and the claim petitioners filed Cross Objections petition No.27 of 2024.

11. Heard arguments submitted by Sri A.Ramakrishna Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for Appellant-Insurance Company I MACMA.No.1711 of 2018 as well as Sri Goli Viplav Reddy, learned counsel for the Respondents/Cross-objectors.

12. The contentions of the learned counsel for appellant/Insurance Company are that the learned Tribunal failed to consider that the driver of the crime vehicle do not have valid driving license and permit to drive the crime Auto and the owner of the said Auto had willfully and knowingly handed United India Insurance Co.Ltd vs Smt.Kandukuribaindlalaxmamma And 5 ... on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145295555/
2 over the crime vehicle to respondent No.1/driver and violated the terms and conditions of Insurance policy.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co.Ltd vs Smt.Kandukuribaindlalaxmamma And 5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It also contended that the Tribunal had wrongly taken the income of the deceased @
Rs.4,500/- per MGP,J MACMA.1711 of 2018 and X-obj.27 of 2024 month and wrongly applied the multiplier and also awarded excess interest @ 9% per annum .
Hence, prayed to allow the Appeal by setting aside the order of the learned Tribunal.

13. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/cross- objectors contended that though the claim petitioners had established their case by adducing cogent and convincing evidence and also by relying upon documents marked under Exs.A1 to A5, but the learned Tribunal, without considering the same, had awarded meager amount towards the income of the deceased, failed to award future prospects to the income of the deceased and hence requested to allow the cross-objection petition by enhancing the compensation amount.

14. Now the points that emerge for consideration are,
(i) Whether the order passed by the learned Tribunal requires interference of this Court?
(i) Whether the cross-objector is entitled for enhancement of compensation?
Points- 15.
It is pertinent to state that there is no dispute regarding occurrence of accident and death of the deceased as evident from the documentary evidence filed under Exs.A1 to A5.

A perusal of Ex.A1 shows that Police of Yacharam Police Station registered a MGP,J MACMA.1711 of 2018 and X-obj.27 of 2024 case in Crime No.65/2011, conducted investigation and filed charge sheet under EX.A2 against the driver of the crime Auto.
Ex.A3 is the Post Mortem Examination report.
Ex.A4 is the Death Certificate of the deceased and Ex.A5 is the scene of offence panchanama along with rough sketch.

Hence, from the above documentary evidence, it is proved that the death of the deceased was due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of crime Auto which finding of the learned Tribunal attains finality and do not require any further interference by this Court.

16. The main contention of the learned counsel for appellant/Insurance Company in M.A.C.M.A.No.1711 of 2018 is that the learned Tribunal failed to see that the driver of the crime vehicle do not have valid driving license and permit to drive the crime Auto at the time of accident and the owner of the said Auto had willfully and knowingly handed over the crime vehicle to respondent No.1/driver and committed breach of the policy conditions.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.

17. In this regard, it is pertinent to refer the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case between S. Iyyapan v/s M/s United India Insurance Company and Another wherein, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the Insurance Company is MGP,J MACMA.1711 of 2018 and X-obj.27 of 2024 liable to pay the victim even if the driver was unlicensed so that the victim should not be deprived of the money due to him.

entities.text: S. Iyyapan v/s M/s United India Insurance Company and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence Insurance Company has full rights to recover their money from the owner of the vehicle.

Further, the owner can make the unlicensed driver to pay the United India Insurance Co.Ltd vs Smt.Kandukuribaindlalaxmamma And 5 ... on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145295555/
3 compensation.
18.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co.Ltd vs Smt.Kandukuribaindlalaxmamma And 5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, RW1- Manager (Legal) examined on behalf of Insurance Company stated in his evidence that the Motor Vehicle Inspector, RTA, Ibrahimpatnam inspected the crime vehicle and mentioned in his report that the driver of the crime vehicle do not have valid Driving license to drive the vehicle at the time of accident and respondent No.1/owner of the vehicle, knowingly handed over the crime vehicle to driver and violated the terms and conditions of Insurance policy.

He also deposed that though the Insurance Company issued notices to the driver and owner requesting to furnish the details of driving license and permit particulars, but they failed to give any reply and thus, they can be held vicariously liable to pay compensation to the claimants.
In support of his evidence he got marked Exs.B1 to B9 on behalf of Insurance Company.
A perusal of Ex.B1- copy of Insurance policy shows that the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Ex.B2 is the MVI report which discloses that the occurrence of accident was not due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle .
MGP,J MACMA.1711 of 2018 and X-obj.27 of 2024
Ex.B3 is the statement of owner of vehicle.
Ex . B4
are the postal receipts.
Ex . B5
is the legal notice issued to driver of vehicle.
Ex . B6
is the acknowledgment card.
Ex . B7
is the notice issued to owner of Auto.
Ex . B8
is the returned registered cover.
Ex . B9
is the Authorization letter.

19. Therefore, from the evidence of RW1, Exs.B3 to B9 and by relying upon the above referred decision, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Insurance Company cannot be exonerated from its liability to pay the compensation amount.
It shall pay the compensation at first and then recover the same from the owner, who in turn can add the unlicensed driver to pay the compensation.

20. So far as cross-objection petition filed by the petitioners is concerned, it is the contention of the learned counsel for petitioners that the learned Tribunal, had awarded meager amount towards the income of the deceased.

In this regard, it is pertinent to state that though the petitioners contended that the deceased used to earn Rs.10,000/- per month as Agricultural labour and also drum beating,
they did not file any documentary proof evidencing the same.

Hence, the Tribunal, taking into consideration the income of an unskilled labour who is able bodied, fixed the income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- which this MGP,J MACMA.1711 of 2018 and X-obj.27 of 2024 Court finds reasonable and is not inclined to interfere with the same.

Since the Tribunal failed to award future prospects to the established income of the deceased, this Court, by relying upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, is inclined to add 40% towards future prospects to the income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence the future monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.6,300/-.

If 1/4th amount is deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased as the number of dependents being four, then the net monthly income comes to Rs.4,725/- and the annual income comes to Rs.56,700/-.
Since the deceased was 30 years old at the time of the accident, the appropriate multiplier is '17' as per the guidelines laid down by the Apex Court in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 1.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the total loss of dependency on account of the death of the deceased comes to Rs.9,63,900/-.
Apart from this, the learned Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.25,000/- towards funeral charges and Rs.5,000/-

4 towards transportation charges which this Court finds to be meager and is inclined to interfere with the same by awarding a sum of Rs.77,000/- under Conventional Heads as per Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (cited supra) .

sentences.text: As far as interest is concerned, the learned Tribunal granted interest @ 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit which this Court considers to be excess and hereby inclined to interfere with the same by reducing the same to 7.5% per annum by relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajesh and others v. Rajbir Singh and others 3.

entities.text: Rajesh and others v. Rajbir Singh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
22. Since the compensation arrived is more than the claim amount, it is pertinent to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case between Nagappa Vs.Gurudayal Singh and others 4 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:-
"...under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, (hereinafter referred to as "the MV Act") there is no restriction that compensation could be awarded only up to the amount claimed by the claimant.
In an appropriate case where from the evidence brought on record if Tribunal/court considers that claimant is entitled to get more compensation than claimed, the Tribunal may pass such award.

Only 3 2013 ACJ 1403 = 2013 (4) ALT 35 AIR 2003 SC 674 MGP,J MACMA.1711 of 2018 and X-obj.27 of 2024 embargo is it should be 'Just' compensation, that is to say, it should be neither arbitrary, fanciful nor unjustifiable from the evidence."
23. With the above finding of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is clear that the compensation can be granted more than the claim made based on cogent and convincing evidence.
24. In view of the above discussion and keeping in view the settled principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this Court deems fit and proper to allow the Appeal.

25. In the result, M.A.C.M.A.No.1711 of 2018 is partly- allowed by reducing the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal from 9% to 7.5% per annum and the Cross-objections petition No.27 of 2024 filed by the claim petitioners is allowed by enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.4,89,000/- to Rs.11,20,900/- which shall carry interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization payable by respondent No. 3 in O.P./Insurance Company in the first instance within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and later recover the same from the respondent No.1/owner of subject Auto, who in turn can add the unlicensed driver to pay the compensation.

Upon such deposit, the claim petitioners are entitled to withdraw the same MGP,J MACMA.1711 of 2018 and X-obj.27 of 2024 as per the apportionment made by the learned Tribunal by foregoing interest for a period of '1590' days as per orders dated 13.09.2024 passed in I.A.No.1 of 2024 and by paying deficit Court fee.
There shall be no order as to costs.
26. Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
